title: Staggered retroprocessing fanout with tenant-priority queue
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Large historical backfills (usage events and aggregated counts) currently run as cluster-wide jobs that either saturate downstream stores or require full-tenant throttles, causing long customer-facing delays and high egress/unit costs. We need a controlled mechanism that can run large-scale retroprocessing while preferentially serving higher-priority tenants and avoiding global resource contention.

Goal: Implement a staggered retroprocessing fanout controller that partitions backfill workloads into tenant-priority queues, supports dynamic concurrency and cost-aware throttling, and provides safe resume checkpoints and cancellation. This should reduce tail impact on shared storage, let platform teams schedule high-value tenant backfills earlier, and provide deterministic, auditable runs with minimal operator intervention.

High-level design decisions:
- Fanout model: produce backfill tasks to a central Kafka "retro-fanout" topic partitioned by tenant namespace and priority bucket. Workers consume with a coordinated lease-based concurrency controller to limit per-tenant parallelism.
- Priority buckets: three buckets (urgent, standard, low). Buckets map to configurable concurrency and cost budgets.
- Staggering strategy: the controller enqueues windows of time (e.g., hourly slices) per-tenant and issues them with backoff windows to avoid hotspotting external datastore (clickhouse/olap).
- Checkpointing: each task carries a monotonic resume cursor (time-window + checksum) persisted to the retroruns store so jobs are idempotent and resumable.
- Safety guardrails: pre-check dry-run estimator that computes projected token/row throughput and cost; abort when > safety threshold.
- Tenant prioritization: priority is derived from Billing tier + manual overrides via Console. UI will expose an admission API for product/SRE to bump a tenant's bucket for a single run.

Acceptance criteria:
- Backfill for a 90-day tenant can complete with no more than 25% increase in observed p95 API latency for a sustained 1-hour window in the shared analytics cluster.
- System supports pausing/resuming runs with resume tokens and can replay from a specific cursor.
- Console exposes run status, cost estimate, and per-tenant progress percentage.
- Dry-run cost estimates are within ±20% of actual for 95% of sampled runs.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Prototype controller & schema (2 wks): design retro-fanout topic schema, implement controller that slices windowed tasks and writes to Kafka; local worker that consumes and logs checkpoints.
2) Safety & estimator (1 wk): implement dry-run estimator using sampling + historic ingestion rates; add cluster-wide safety checks.
3) Worker scaling & concurrency (2 wks): build lease-based concurrency limiter, per-tenant quotas and dynamic backoff.
4) Console integration & admission API (1 wk): UI endpoints for manual priority bump, run cancellation, and progress UX.
5) Observability & runbooks (1 wk): dashboards, SLO checks, and incident runbook.

Trade-offs considered:
- Kafka vs SQS: Kafka chosen for efficient partitioned fanout and ability to retain task history for audit. This increases operator complexity but gives better throughput.
- Strong consistency for checkpoints vs eventual: we opt for checkpoint writes to a strongly-consistent store (Postgres) to avoid duplicate reprocessing at expense of higher write load; mitigations include batching checkpoint writes.
- Per-tenant isolation vs utilization: strict isolation reduces impact but can leave capacity idle. We introduce a borrow pool that can be temporarily used by low-priority tenants when utilization is low.

Observability & Metrics:
- new metrics: retro.tasks.enqueued, retro.tasks.started, retro.tasks.completed, retro.tasks.failed, retro.checkpoint.latency, retro.cost.tenant.<tenant_id>.estimated, retro.lease.contention, retro.window.backoff_seconds.
- Dashboards: "Retroprocessing Overview" (Run counts, cost burn-down, hot tenants), "Per-Tenant Progress" (progress bars, ETA), and alert rules for checkpoint failures > 5% and estimated cost vs budget > 30%. Link: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/retro/retro-overview

Runbook & safety:
- Automatic pauses triggered when cluster p95 API latency increases > 10% over baseline.
- Manual cancellation via Console button + API (POST /retro/runs/{id}/cancel).
- Operators can expedite a tenant by bumping priority or increasing concurrency through a controlled feature flag.

Artifacts & references:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ANALY/Staggered+Retroprocessing+Fanout
- Prototype code (feature branch): https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/tree/retro-fanout-prototype
- Example PR (worker): https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/pull/2891
- Console ticket for admission UI: PM-4129

Security & compliance notes:
- Tasks must avoid shipping raw PII. The producer will include hashed identifiers; any rehydration will run in a tenant-scoped VPC-only path where required.
- No keys or secrets are embedded in tasks; workers use instance role to read encrypted checkpoints from Postgres.

Rollout plan:
- Canary: 5 low-impact tenants for initial end-to-end run; monitor dashboard and latency impact for 48h.
- Stage: enable for a cohort of 50 tenants with mixed tiers; run cost estimation and iterate.
- GA: open to all tenants with default low priority and opt-in for urgent runs.

Open questions / blocked items:
- Need SRE sign-off on Kafka retention and topic partitioning strategy (cost vs throughput).
- Finalize exact mapping of Billing tier -> default priority buckets.
- Decide if borrow pool should be global or per-region (affects cross-region data access).

Next actions (short-term):
- Miguel: land prototype controller that writes windowed tasks to retro-fanout topic (ETA 2025-02-14).
- Aisha: complete dry-run estimator spec and dataset sampling query (ETA 2025-02-18).
- SRE (requested): run Kafka partitioning options analysis by 2025-02-21.

Notes: This ticket focuses on backend runtime and orchestration. Follow-up tickets will address cost-recovery labels, billing visibility, and a UI polish epic for rich run history and CSV export.
